parameters.content:
## 🤖 AI ERP Office Assistant — sample

Chat with an AI agent that does real office work in your ERP (ERPNext): customer / item / stock lookups, receivables, draft invoices, leave applications and email.

### Setup (~10 min)
**1. Model** — open *Claude (Anthropic)* and select your Anthropic API credential (or swap in any other chat-model node).

**2. ERP URL** — replace `your-company.erpnext.com` with your ERPNext address in all 7 HTTP tools.

**3. ERP auth** — create one **Header Auth** credential and select it in every HTTP tool:
• Name: `Authorization`
• Value: `token <api_key>:<api_secret>`
(Generate the key pair in ERPNext under **User → Settings → API Access**.)

**4. Email** — connect a Gmail account in *send_email* (or replace it with SMTP / Outlook).

Then open **Chat** below the canvas and try the example prompts →

### Not on ERPNext?
Point the HTTP tools at your ERP's own REST API instead (Odoo JSON-RPC, Dolibarr, Zoho Books, SAP B1 Service Layer…). Only the URLs, auth and field names change — the agent pattern stays the same.

### Different trigger?
Swap the Chat Trigger for a Gmail / Slack / Telegram / WhatsApp trigger so employees can message the assistant where they already work.

### 💬 Try asking

• "Which customers do we have in the Retail group?"
• "How much stock of SKU-0001 is left, per warehouse?"
• "List all overdue invoices and total the outstanding amount."
• "Create an invoice for Acme Corp: 5 × SKU-0001 at 1200 each, due end of next month."
• "File casual leave for Priya from the 3rd to the 5th of next month."
• "Email an overdue-payment reminder for ACC-SINV-2026-00042 to billing@acme.com."

⚠️ Safe by design: invoices and leave are created as **Draft / Open**, and the agent asks for confirmation before every write or email.

### 🔎 Read-only ERP tools
Lookups against the ERPNext REST API — `GET /api/resource/<Doctype>` with `fields` and `filters` query params.

### ✍️ Write & comms tools
Documents are created as Drafts via `POST /api/resource/<Doctype>` — a human still reviews and submits them in the ERP. Email goes out via Gmail.

options.systemMessage:
=You are Ava, the AI office assistant for a small enterprise that runs its business on ERPNext. Today is {{ $now.format('yyyy-MM-dd') }}.

You take care of everyday office work using your tools:
- Look up customers, items and employees
- Check live warehouse stock
- List sales invoices and summarise receivables
- Create DRAFT sales invoices
- File leave applications
- Send emails on request

Ground rules:
1. Facts come from tools. Never invent customers, item codes, stock figures or amounts. Always resolve human names to exact IDs (search_customers, search_items, list_employees) before any write action.
2. Before every write action (create_sales_invoice, create_leave_application, send_email), show a short summary of exactly what you are about to do and wait for the user's explicit confirmation.
3. ERPNext conventions: dates are YYYY-MM-DD; the "filters" query parameter is a JSON array like [["field","=","value"]]; use document IDs exactly as the API returned them.
4. Documents you create are Draft (invoices) or Open (leave applications) — remind the user that a person still reviews and submits them in ERPNext.
5. If a lookup returns nothing, say so and suggest the closest likely match.
6. Keep replies brief and business-like; use a compact markdown table when listing more than three records.
7. Anything outside your tools (payments, payroll, deletions, master-data changes) must be done manually in ERPNext — say so politely.

parameters.toolDescription: Search customers (ERPNext Customer doctype). Returns name (the customer ID), customer_name, customer_group and territory. To narrow results, pass the optional 'filters' query parameter as a JSON array, e.g. [["customer_name","like","%acme%"]] or [["customer_group","=","Retail"]]. Call without filters to list the first 20 customers.

Search products / items (ERPNext Item doctype). Returns name (the item code), item_name, item_group, stock_uom and standard_rate. Optional 'filters' query parameter as a JSON array, e.g. [["item_name","like","%chair%"]]. Use this to resolve exact item codes before creating an invoice.

Check live warehouse stock (ERPNext Bin doctype). Returns item_code, warehouse and actual_qty. The 'filters' query parameter is REQUIRED and must be a JSON array, e.g. [["item_code","=","SKU-0001"]] to see one item across all warehouses, or [["warehouse","=","Stores - ACM"]] for everything in one warehouse.

List sales invoices (ERPNext Sales Invoice doctype). Returns name (invoice ID), customer, posting_date, due_date, status, grand_total, outstanding_amount and currency. Optional 'filters' query parameter as a JSON array — unpaid/overdue only: [["status","in",["Unpaid","Overdue"]]]; one customer: [["customer","=","CUST-00001"]]. Statuses include Draft, Unpaid, Overdue, Paid, Cancelled.

Look up employees (ERPNext Employee doctype) — use this to resolve the employee ID before filing a leave application. Returns name (employee ID like HR-EMP-00001), employee_name, department, designation and status. Optional 'filters' query parameter as a JSON array, e.g. [["employee_name","like","%priya%"]].

Create a new DRAFT sales invoice in the ERP. First resolve the exact customer ID (search_customers) and item codes (search_items), confirm the details with the user, then call this tool. The invoice is saved as a Draft for human review — it is not submitted or emailed automatically. Returns the created document including its new invoice ID.

values.name: invoice
values.description: The Sales Invoice as a JSON object: {"customer": "<customer ID from search_customers>", "due_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "items": [{"item_code": "<item code from search_items>", "qty": <number>, "rate": <unit price as number>}]}

parameters.toolDescription: File a leave application for an employee (created with status Open, pending HR approval). First resolve the employee ID with list_employees and confirm the dates and leave type with the user, then call this tool. Returns the created leave application document.

values.name: leave
values.description: The Leave Application as a JSON object: {"employee": "<employee ID from list_employees>", "leave_type": "<e.g. Casual Leave, Sick Leave, Privilege Leave>", "from_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "to_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "status": "Open"}
